title: The Holiness of God
overview: Psalm 99 is a majestic declaration of God's sovereign reign and holiness. It emphasizes the fear and reverence due to the LORD as the exalted King who dwells between the cherubim, highlighting His supreme authority over all the earth. The psalm calls the people to worship God at His holy mountain, Zion, recognizing His justice, righteousness, and mercy. It recalls the faithful intercession of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel, illustrating God’s responsiveness to prayer and His forgiving nature despite His righteous judgment. This chapter serves as a powerful reminder of God's holiness, justice, and the proper response of worship and reverence, anchoring the believer’s trust in His righteous rule and grace.
structure:
**Verses 1-3: The Sovereignty and Holiness of God.** The psalm opens with a proclamation of God's reign and the awe it inspires, emphasizing His presence between the cherubim and His exalted position in Zion. The people are called to tremble and praise His holy name.

**Verses 4-5: God’s Justice and Worship.** These verses focus on God's love for justice and righteousness, highlighting His role as a righteous King who establishes equity. The people are exhorted to exalt and worship God at His footstool, acknowledging His holiness.

**Verses 6-8: The Faithful Intercessors and God’s Response.** The psalm recalls the prayers of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel, emphasizing their calling on the LORD and His faithful answers. It also references God's communication through the cloudy pillar and His forgiveness despite taking vengeance on sin.

**Verse 9: Final Call to Worship.** The psalm concludes with a renewed call to exalt and worship God at His holy hill, reaffirming the central theme of God's holiness.

keyVerses.text: The LORD reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved.
keyVerses.significance: This verse establishes God's supreme authority and majestic presence, inspiring reverence and awe. It sets the tone for the entire psalm by affirming God's reign and the appropriate human response of trembling before Him.

keyVerses.text: The king's strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights God's character as a just and righteous King who loves and establishes equity. It underscores the biblical theme that God's reign is marked by moral justice and fairness.

keyVerses.text: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name; they called upon the LORD, and he answered them.
keyVerses.significance: This verse connects the psalm to Israel’s history of faithful leaders who interceded for the people. It emphasizes God’s responsiveness to prayer and the importance of calling upon His name.

keyVerses.text: Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at his holy hill; for the LORD our God is holy.
keyVerses.significance: The closing verse reiterates the central theme of God's holiness and calls for worship. It reminds believers that reverence and exaltation of God are appropriate responses to His holy nature.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: The sovereign God who reigns over all, enthroned between the cherubim. He is holy, just, and merciful, executing judgment and righteousness in Israel.

characters.name: Moses
characters.description: A key intercessor and leader of Israel, representing faithful prayer and obedience. He called upon the LORD and received answers, exemplifying God’s covenant relationship with His people.

characters.name: Aaron
characters.description: Brother of Moses and high priest, symbolizing the priestly role in calling upon God and mediating between God and Israel.

characters.name: Samuel
characters.description: A prophet and priest who called upon the LORD, demonstrating faithful leadership and God’s readiness to answer His people’s prayers.

themes.description: The psalm emphasizes God’s supreme reign over all creation, calling for reverence and submission. This theme aligns with the broader biblical teaching of God as King over all the earth.
God’s holiness is central, described as ‘holy’ and ‘terrible’ in His majesty. The call to worship at His holy hill underscores the necessity of reverence and purity before Him.
God’s love for judgment and equity highlights His moral perfection and governance. This theme connects to the biblical narrative of God as the righteous judge who upholds justice.
The remembrance of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel’s prayers illustrates God’s faithfulness in answering His people, encouraging believers to call upon Him with confidence.
The psalm repeatedly calls for exaltation and worship of God, emphasizing the proper human response to His holiness and kingship.

historicalContext: Psalm 99 likely originates from the post-exilic period when the Israelites were reestablishing worship in Jerusalem, emphasizing God's reign from Zion, the holy mountain. The imagery of God enthroned between the cherubim reflects the Ark of the Covenant’s presence in the temple, a central symbol of God's dwelling among His people. The mention of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel connects the psalm to Israel's historical leaders who mediated between God and the people, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant faithfulness despite Israel's past failures. Politically, this period was marked by Persian rule, allowing the Jews limited autonomy to rebuild their temple and worship practices.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God’s absolute sovereignty and holiness as revealed in this psalm. The call to worship and fear God aligns with the doctrine of God’s majesty and justice, underscoring human dependence on divine grace.

Dispensational interpreters see Psalm 99 as highlighting God’s kingdom rule from Zion, foreshadowing the millennial reign of Christ. The references to historical priests and prophets illustrate God’s unfolding plan of redemption through distinct dispensations.

Early church fathers often interpreted the psalm Christologically, seeing the LORD enthroned as a prefiguration of Christ’s heavenly kingship and priestly intercession, with Moses, Aaron, and Samuel as types of Christ’s mediatorial role.

application: Approach God with reverence and awe, recognizing His sovereign reign over all aspects of life.
Commit to worshiping God regularly, especially remembering His holiness and justice.
Trust in God’s faithfulness to answer prayer as He did for Moses, Aaron, and Samuel.
Pursue justice and righteousness in your own life, reflecting God’s character.
Remember that God’s holiness calls for personal holiness and obedience.
Exalt God in community worship, acknowledging His presence among His people.
conclusion: Psalm 99 powerfully affirms the holiness and sovereign reign of God, calling believers to a posture of reverence, worship, and trust. By recalling the faithful intercessions of Israel’s leaders and God’s righteous judgment, the psalm encourages believers to approach God with awe and confidence. Its timeless message challenges Christians today to honor God’s justice, embrace His holiness, and faithfully call upon His name, knowing He is a gracious and righteous King who reigns eternally.
timeline: c. 6th century BC - Post-Exilic Period during the restoration of Jerusalem and the Temple

outline.heading: God’s Sovereign Reign and Holiness
outline.description: The psalm opens by declaring the LORD’s reign and His presence between the cherubim, calling the people to tremble and praise His holy name.

outline.heading: God’s Justice and Call to Worship
outline.description: These verses highlight God’s love for justice and righteousness and exhort the people to worship Him at His footstool, recognizing His holiness.

outline.heading: Faithful Intercessors and God’s Response
outline.description: The psalm recalls the prayers of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel, emphasizing God’s communication and forgiveness despite His righteous judgment.

outline.heading: Final Exhortation to Worship
outline.description: The psalm concludes with a renewed call to exalt and worship the LORD at His holy hill, reaffirming His holiness as the foundation for worship.
